note: Human adjudications of MIW topic mappings. This file is HAND-MAINTAINED and is an INPUT to build_study_mappings.py -- never edit docs/study/study_mappings.json directly. Three decisions are available. AFFIRM (the default) promotes one mapping to VALID_MAPPED by supplying the review stamp the validator demands. REASSIGN moves a question the mapper placed wrongly, and must also carry mapper_topic_id. HOLD_REVIEW records that a human read the question and found the evidence did not settle it: the mapping is forced to REVIEW_PENDING with candidate_topic_ids, and is never published. In every case the mapper's own current topic must be RESTATED (mapper_topic_id, defaulting to topic_id) so a taxonomy change that moves the question is caught rather than silently rubber-stamped.

QB4_G#q1.note: Verbatim candidate-submitted wording, typo included, on the flag State versus Recognised Organisation split. Same subject as QB4_A#q8. D01. Confirmed NOT a truncation defect: the stored index text and the source HTML agree exactly.

QB4_G#q5.note: Dry dock preparation as CE plus the dry dock interval. QB2_A#q11.note: Grain Code. QB2_A#q15.note: International Certificate of Fitness. This is NOT the blanket 'certificate means D01' move warned against: the stem asks the certification questions directly.

QB2_A#q24.note: Digital inclinometer. SOLAS V/20 carriage requirement for container ships and bulk carriers of 3,000 GT and above; MEMS sensing, roll period and VDR logging, early warning of parametric and synchronous rolling. The subject is stability monitoring, D10. Not a cargo question at all.

QB2_A#q25.note: Persistent floater. Defined by the GESAMP hazard profile and operative only through MARPOL Annex II -- Category Y pre-wash and shore reception in the North Sea and Baltic zones. A pollution-prevention question about a cargo, D04.

QB6_D#q2.note: Azimuth propeller working principle: pod, Z/L-drive transmission, 360-degree thrust vectoring, multi-barrier shaft seals, steering gear hydraulics. Propulsion machinery, D09. The D10 cue fired on the bare word 'propeller' -- a vocabulary false positive. File topic affirmed.

QB6_D#q3.note: EGR versus SCR, and which is commercially better. Machinery, D09. File topic affirmed.

QB6_D#q4.note: NOx formation and demonstrating compliance with no gas analyser fitted. The combustion-chemistry limb is preparatory; the operative limb -- and the whole point of the question -- is the verification regime: MARPOL Annex VI regulation 13, the EIAPP Certificate, the NOx Technical File, NOx Technical Code Chapter 6 and the Engine Parameter Check method, recorded in the Record Book of Engine Parameters and checked at survey. A regulatory question wearing machinery vocabulary, D04.

QB6_D#q5.note: Cavitation in a centrifugal pump and on a propeller. Engine room and propulsion machinery practice, D09. The D10 cue fired on 'propeller'. File topic affirmed.

QB1_D#q3.note: Lifting appliance survey. Survey cycle plus statutory register plus RO witness -- D01 on all three counts.

QB1_D#q4.note: Load Line survey documents. The answer is the International Load Line Certificate and the Record of Conditions of Assignment, used as the surveyor's checklist. This is the certificate and its survey, not the freeboard calculation -- contrast QB1_D#q5, reassigned to D10 in this same tranche because there the calculation IS the question.

QB1_D#q5.note: Fresh Water Allowance -- what it is, how it is derived, and how it is applied in dock water. The answer is FWA = displacement / (4 x TPC) from Load Line Reg 40, the Fresh and Tropical Fresh marks, and the Dock Water Allowance scaled by density. The instrument is statutory but the examinable content is a hydrostatic calculation, so D10 owns it. Follows QB2_A#q24, where a SOLAS V/20 carriage requirement was still reassigned to D10 because the substance was naval architecture. The D01 cue fired on 'load line'; the D10 cue never ran because D01 precedes it.

QB1_F#q4.note: CSC Convention 1972 -- design type testing, the Safety Approval Plate, PES/ACEP schemes, container types and reefer testing differences. QB1_F#q6.note: Sustainable fuel certificates -- Proof of Sustainability, ISCC/RedCert accredited bodies, feedstock traceability, lifecycle GHG savings, EU ETS and FuelEU Maritime. The D01 cue fired on 'certificate' alone -- exactly the 'it sounds regulatory' move the settlement rule forbids.

QB1_F#q8.note: Hull survey. HSSC framework, close-up survey, UTM, NDT, and the twice-in-five-years bottom survey. Survey regime, not hull design -- consistent with QB3_A#q11 and #q12 (steel plate renewal and substantial corrosion), both adjudicated to D01 because the operative subject is the survey acceptance criteria.

QB1_F#q13.note: Audit, survey, inspection and statutory survey -- definitions and differences. This is the compliance-monitoring architecture itself, which D01's rationale names outright. The ISM audit appears only as the term being contrasted.

QB1_F#q14.note: Types of survey under HSSC, and what CSM is. Class and statutory survey cycles. D01.

QB1_F#q15.note: Items a Chief Engineer cannot credit under the Continuous Machinery Survey scheme. The machinery is the object; the question is about the limits of the CE's delegated class credit, which is class survey administration. D01, not D09.

QB1_F#q16.note: 'explain ESP..' -- verbatim candidate wording, not a truncated index entry (source HTML checked byte-for-byte this session). The answer is the Enhanced Survey Programme under the ESP Code and SOLAS XI-1. Follows QB3_A#q6 and #q7, both adjudicated to D01.

QB1_G#q30.note: 'Esp complete' -- verbatim candidate wording, source HTML verified. Enhanced Survey Programme, ESP Code, SOLAS XI-1/2. Same subject as QB1_F#q16 and QB1_I#q1 and the same precedent (QB3_A#q6/#q7). D01.

QB1_G#q31.note: In-water survey in lieu of drydock bottom survey: the IWS class notation, hull markings, diver/ROV requirements and tailshaft clearance measurement. An alternative survey arrangement under class rules and HSSC. D01.

QB1_G#q34.note: Certificate of Fitness -- contents and details. Direct precedent: QB2_A#q15, where the International Certificate of Fitness was REASSIGNED from D07 to D01 on 2026-08-23 because the stem asked the certification questions directly. It does so here too (issuing authority, survey basis, contents). The IBC Code cargo list is the technical backdrop, not the question.

QB1_G#q36.note: Class Quarterly Listing -- contents, significance and CE actions. Near-duplicate of QB3_A#q17 (class quarterly listing and survey status report, and how the CE uses it), adjudicated to D01 on 2026-08-23.

QB1_G#q40.note: CSM -- concept, application and what is assessed. Same class survey scheme as QB1_F#q14 and #q15. D01.

QB1_H#q1.note: IACS PR 17 -- the RO surveyor's duty, on finding deficiencies during a class or statutory survey, to judge whether they indicate an SMS failure and report to the ISM-issuing organisation. The actor is the class surveyor and the trigger is a class/statutory survey, so the operative subject is the RO/class interface that D01's rationale names. The ISM audit is the downstream consequence, not the question. Contrast QB1_H#q2, reassigned to D03 in this same tranche.

QB1_H#q2.note: IACS PR 9 -- how ROs plan, conduct and report ISM audits: minimum audit durations by ship type, auditor qualification, cross-rank interviews, and the Observation / NC / Major NC escalation with CAP via the DPA and the 3-month additional audit. D03's rationale states that the audit regime is D03 and that it sits ON the statutory certification regime; this question is the audit regime itself. A candidate must answer it from ISM audit mechanics, not from class rules. Split from QB1_H#q1 deliberately: PR 17 is a surveyor's duty at survey, PR 9 is the conduct of the audit.

QB1_I#q1.note: The ESP Code in full -- A.1049(27), mandatory through SOLAS XI-1/2 by MSC.325(90), applying to bulk carriers of 500 GT and above and oil tankers of 5,000 GT and above. Survey programme under the statutory and class regime. Follows QB3_A#q6.

QB1_I#q4.note: Anniversary date of a certificate -- SOLAS I/2(n) and the HSSC survey windows it defines. Statutory certification architecture, D01 core.

QB1_I#q6.note: IACS functions -- Unified Requirements, Unified Interpretations and quality certification of member societies. Follows QB4_E#q12 (IACS member societies), adjudicated to D01 on 2026-08-23. Classification system governance.

QB1_J#q1.note: Hull paint coating inspection during drydock: ISO 8501-1 Sa2.5 blast cleanliness, anchor profile, steel temperature above dew point, wet and dry film thickness gauging, holiday detection. D10 owns hull structure and construction. The D01 cue fired on 'drydock'.

QB1_J#q2.note: Propeller securing/locking arrangement inspection during drydock: fairwater cone removal, hydraulic push-up length verified by dial gauge against the Von Mises criterion, locking plate or wire locking, alignment marks, cone repacking. Propulsion shafting practice -- D09. This is NOT a D10 'propeller' pull: SKILL.md already records the bare word propeller dragging machinery questions into D10 wrongly (QB6_D azimuth propeller), and QB6_D#q5 was affirmed to D09 for the same reason. Here D01 won on 'drydock' before either cue ran.

QB1_K#q1.note: Qualifications to become a Class auditor. The governing instrument is the RO Code Part 2 (MSC.349(92)/MEPC.237(65)): the RO's duty to define competency criteria, train, examine and individually authorise each auditor per scheme. Follows QB1_B#q7, where RO Code criteria for becoming a Recognised Organisation were reassigned to D01. The ISM/ISPS/MLC schemes are what the auditor is authorised FOR, not the subject of the question.

QB1_K#q8.note: 'What is CSR?' -- the answer is unambiguous: IACS Common Structural Rules for Bulk Carriers and Oil Tankers, hull scantling design rules, 90 m bulk carriers and 150 m double-hull tankers contracted on or after 1 July 2015. This is ship construction and naval architecture, D10. The D01 cue matched CSR, a pattern written for the Continuous Synopsis Record (SOLAS XI-1/5, adjudicated to D01 as QB4_C#q4). A genuine cue collision between two unrelated instruments sharing an acronym; recorded as a blind spot rather than patched, since editing the cue table would be a taxonomy change.

QB1_supplementary#q1.note: CE's ISM survey duties in the engine room, expressly beyond documentation and machinery checks. The answer is SOLAS IX, SMS implementation in practice, ISM Section 9 defect reporting, Section 6 familiarisation, and proving a working safety culture. D03 owns ISM and the human element outright. The stem's own wording rules out the survey/hardware reading that the D01 cue assumed.

QB1_supplementary#q6.note: IOPP survey preparation. The answer is MARPOL Annex I throughout: 15 ppm bilge alarm calibration, the automatic stopping device and 3-way divert valve, sludge pump, Oil Record Book Part I against tank soundings, and the magic-pipe risk. Pollution prevention equipment and its record book -- D04. The survey is the setting; MARPOL Annex I is the subject.

QB1_supplementary#q7.note: NOx Technical File -- MARPOL Annex VI Reg 13, engine-specific approved emission settings, the EIAPP certificate, Tier I/II/III, and SCR/EGR mode in a NECA. D04's cue names NOx explicitly. Follows QB6_D#q4, where the NOx compliance question was reassigned to D04. Not D05: this is Annex VI air pollution, not EEXI/CII decarbonisation.

QB10_B#q8.note: Recent DG Shipping / DGMA (India) circulars an Indian MEO Class 1 candidate should know -- DGS Order 01 of 2026 on Indian-flag age norms under MS Act Sec 406/407, MS Notice 01 of 2026 on RPSL empanelment, and DGMA Circulars 17 and 33 of 2026. Every instrument is an Indian administration instrument, which is exactly what D06 exists for. Follows QB4_E#q13 (ship registration in India) and QB9_D#q6 (MS Act). As recorded there, QUESTION_CUES has NO D06 pattern at all, so the detector is structurally unable to name this destination and proposed D01 instead.

QB3_I#q5.note: Biocide-free antifouling paint chemistry. The cue fired D01 on 'class ... approved', but approval by a society does not make a question about classification. Antifouling is named in D04's own rationale (AFS), and the file is the AFS Convention file. Distinguished from QB1_J#q1 (hull paint coating INSPECTION during drydock, reassigned to D10): that question is a coating-application and surface-preparation standard, this one is the AFS-driven chemistry.

QB5_B#q15.note: Risk assessment and Permit to Work for a portable Framo submersible cargo pump. The cue fired D07 on 'cargo pump', but the examinable subject is the SMS HIRARC framework and permit control -- D03 outright. The equipment named in a stem does not own the question; see QB6_F#q2, where the same Framo keyword was affirmed to D09 for the opposite reason.

QB5_C_A#q8.note: Dali incident and CE accountability. The cue fired D02 on 'liability', but the answer is ISM Code and SOLAS II-1 management accountability -- safety barriers, breaker coordination, emergency generator auto-start logic -- not marine insurance or carriage of goods. Follows QB9_H#q6 (company evaluation and MLC assurance is human element, not commercial law).

QB5_D#q2.note: Women's empowerment at sea. Near-duplicate of QB1_B#q21, human-adjudicated to D03 on 2026-08-23 ('IMO gender-equality initiatives are a human-element and industry workforce subject'). The cue fired D01 on 'flag State'; a flag State appears in the stem of much of this corpus and cannot by itself carry a question into the statutory domain.

QB5_H#q2.note: Unfamiliar main engine on joining as CE. The cue fired D09 on 'main engine', but nothing about the engine is examined -- the subject is structured familiarisation, the SMS familiarisation checklist and escalating a competence gap. D03. The mirror image of QB6_F#q2.

QB6#q5.note: The greenhouse gas basket under MARPOL Annex VI and whether water vapour qualifies. The cue fired D04 on 'MARPOL', but the instrument cited is Annex VI Chapter 4, which is the GHG chapter and is exactly what D05 was created to hold. A MARPOL citation does not settle D04 against D05; the chapter does.

QB6_F#q2.note: Latest developments in Framo hydraulic cargo pumping technology. The cue fired D07 on 'cargo pumping', but the content is VFD-driven power packs, condition monitoring and hydraulic plant -- D09's stated remit of engine-room practice and new technology. Paired with QB5_B#q15, which carries the same Framo keyword and stays in D03.

QB7_E#q2.note: Can cargo be used as fuel, and which code governs. Genuinely touches D07, but the examined subject is the FUEL arrangement -- IGF Code, the SOLAS low-flashpoint provisions, and boil-off gas under the IGC Code. Using a cargo as fuel is an alternative-fuels question, which is D05's remit. Not held: unlike QB9_B#q8 this is one subject reached through two instruments, not two subjects.

QB7_I#q7.note: Wind-Assisted Propulsion Systems and adoption status. The cue fired D09 on 'propulsion', but the answer's whole frame is fuel and emissions saving, CII rating improvement and EU ETS cost avoidance. Decarbonisation technology is D05; D09 would claim it only if the question examined the rotor plant itself.

QB9_C#q4.note: Oil tanker liabilities and the applicable conventions. The cue fired D07 on 'oil tanker', which is the cargo the ship carries, not the subject of the question. CLC 1992, the Fund Convention, P&I cover and personal criminal exposure for the ORB are marine liability -- D02 verbatim.

QB1_B#q5.note: Continuous Synopsis Record: what it is and what entries it carries. Near-duplicate of QB4_C#q4, human-adjudicated to D01 on 2026-08-23 as a flag-issued statutory history document. SOLAS XI-1/5 -- statutory framework, not commercial law. The standing 'CSR is ambiguous' caution does not bite here: the stem expands the acronym itself.

QB2_F#q1.note: Latest amendments governing carriage of IMDG cargo -- Amendment 42-24, the EmS Guide Rev.3, DoC segregation limits. D07's rationale names IMDG explicitly. The file title advertises fire safety and LSA, and the fire limb here is incidental to a carriage-of-dangerous-goods question under SOLAS VII.

QB2_G#q1.note: Timber and log deck cargo and its precautions. Governed by the 2011 TDC Code and a Timber Load Line assignment; the enhanced 2008 IS Code criteria are the precautions the stem asks for, not the subject. Cargo carriage -- D07. D10 was considered and rejected: the stability criteria are cited as a condition of carriage, not examined as naval architecture.

QB2_I#q7.note: What is the IGC Code. D07's rationale names IGC by name. Construction and equipment standards for gas carriers under SOLAS VII. Distinguished from QB2_A#q15 (the International Certificate of Fitness itself, reassigned to D01): there the subject was the certificate, its issuer and its survey cycle; here it is the cargo code.

QB3_H#q3.note: Testing the high and low-low level alarms on the inert gas system. The mapper's D04 is wrong -- an IG plant is not pollution prevention -- but the cue's proposed D07 is wrong too. Inert gas systems are FSS Code Chapter 15 under SOLAS II-2, which is D08. A worked instance of the standing caution that the contradiction cue identifies a bad assignment without identifying the right one.

QB3_J#q2.note: Carbon footprint and how it is measured on board. Fuel consumption times Cf, reported through the IMO DCS (Annex VI Reg.27) and expressed as attained CII (Reg.28). CII, DCS and SEEMP are D05's stated remit; the MARPOL citation is Annex VI, which does not keep it in D04. The same Annex VI reasoning as QB6#q5, applied in the other direction.

QB4_B#q4.note: Documents a Chief Engineer must have ready for class and statutory surveys. Survey preparation, following QB4_G#q5 (drydock preparation as CE, reassigned to D01) and QB4_A#q10 (statutory certification, D01). The ISM tag reflects where the file lives, not what is examined.

QB5_C_B#q8.note: Two meanings of CSR and the CSR/E-CSR difference. Two of the three limbs are statutory -- the Continuous Synopsis Record under SOLAS XI-1/5 and its electronic form -- and the Corporate Social Responsibility limb is a one-line definitional contrast, not a management question. Primary ownership D01, consistent with QB4_C#q4 and QB1_B#q5. The third CSR meaning that sent QB1_K#q8 to D10 (IACS Common Structural Rules) is not raised by this stem.

QB5_G#q3.note: DRI cargo hazards. Terse candidate wording, verified against the card and genuine -- not truncated. Direct Reduced Iron under the IMSBC Code, Group B chemical hazard and Group M liquefaction, hydrogen evolution and self-heating. D07's rationale names IMSBC. Nothing human-element about it; it sits in a management file by accident of authoring.

QB8_B#q3.note: Smart / electronic Bill of Lading, its legal status and framework. The B/L is the carriage-of-goods document -- receipt, evidence of the contract of carriage and document of title under the UNCITRAL MLETR. D02's rationale names carriage of goods. Here the cue is right and the file title is what is wrong.

QB8_F#q2.note: Frame stripping and purging after a scavenge space fire. The mapper's D07 is wrong -- there is no cargo in this question -- but the cue's D08 is also wrong: a scavenge fire is not an FSS or LSA subject. Stopping the engine, engaging turning gear, isolating scavenge air and drains, and purging before re-entry is engine-room practice, which is D09. The same detector failure mode as QB3_H#q3, resolved the other way.

QB9_F#q4.note: Fraudulent registration of ships. Registry, the right to fly a flag and the UNCLOS genuine-link architecture. Follows the QB1_A#q19-q23 line, all reassigned from D02 to D01 on 2026-08-23 as flag and coastal State jurisdiction. Distinguished from QB4_E#q13 (ship registration in India, reassigned to D06): this stem is the international regime, with no Merchant Shipping Act limb.

QB9_G#q1.note: Indian Acts beyond the Merchant Shipping Act -- Admiralty Act 2017, Recycling of Ships Act 2019, Major Port Authorities Act 2021, Marine Insurance Act 1963 -- and the contents of the Admiralty Act. Indian maritime legislation, which is what D06 exists for; follows QB9_D#q6. The cue proposed D04 off 'Recycling of Ships'; D06 has no cue in the engine at all, so the detector could not have proposed the right answer here.

QB9_H#q13.note: Which certificates the CE manages, and reading the current SMS revision. The dominant limb is the statutory certificate inventory -- CSSC machinery scope, IOPP and supplement, IAPP and EIAPP, BWM, ISPP, load line and tonnage -- which is D01, following QB4_A#q10. The SMS limb is answered in the negative ('not from the certificate') and is a corrective aside, not a second subject.

QB9_H#q2.note: Ship casualty response and how the flag State conducts its process. The Casualty Investigation Code MSC.255(84), mandatory through SOLAS XI-1/6, plus the DGMA and MS Act inquiry machinery. Distinguished from the QB1_A#q24 HOLD on the same instrument: there the stem expressly asked for the human elements and so carried a real D03 limb, whereas this stem asks for the flag State's process by name. The statutory limb is the one examined.

QB3_C#q2.note: 'Oil tanker amendment package?' is a current-affairs sweep, not a cargo question -- the cue's D07 is a false lead off 'oil tanker'. The content splits across SOLAS II-2 flashpoint declarations under MSC.520(106), MARPOL Annex VI EEXI/CII, and STCW/MLC endorsements and financial security, with no limb dominant and no way to know from the stem which an examiner would pursue. Held on the QB1_A#q30 ('MEPC 84 outcomes') precedent rather than forced.

QB9_B#q8.note: Medical evacuation and diversion. Genuinely two-limbed with an explicit commercial limb the stem asks for by name: the MLC free telemedical entitlement and shipowner liability for care and repatriation (D03) against off-hire and P&I recovery (D02). Directly follows QB9_B#q2, held in the same file on 2026-08-23 for the same limb-level reason. Not forced.
